chapter: Discovering Henderson, clarinet and first gigs
title: Lieutenant Mikell and the 369th Cadet Boys Band
summary: Procope explains the Mikell name, Mikell's sons, and how Mikell formed the cadet band after Jim Europe's death and offered him a clarinet place; he recalls Buster Bailey as a hero.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Well, it was '25, then, whatever it was. Whatever it was. So -- well, it ties in about this Mikell, Mikell, yeah, that's what Stanley Dance's name is. We used to call him Michael.
I don't know why everybody called him -- we used to call him Professor Michael, or Lieutenant.

Well, we still said Michael. And now his son -- I went to school with his son Gene. Gene, he was a musician, he played with the Mills Blue Rythm Band at the Cotton Club, and he had an older brother, Otto Mikell. He was a saxophone player too. He played saxophone and cello. He died recently over in Montclair, New Jersey. And, well, I don't want to stray. Getting back to the -- but then this Mikell, he started the 369th Cadet Boys Band, see. He got the idea to, because he was the band leader of the 15th Regiment Band after Jim Europe was killed.

See, then he took over the band. He was a Lieutenant. So then -- so it tied in. So I said to him, I said, "Well, I can't join the band. I'm a violin player. I can't march with a violin." So he says, "Well, I tell you what. There's clarinet players that we need," and he said, "Would you like to play?" I said, "Oh, yeah," because I'd seen Buster Bailey up there with this clarinet. Buster Bailey was one of my heroes, and he still is, because I think Buster Bailey, regardless of what anyone says about Buster Bailey Buster Bailey was the best clarinet player I ever knew. And I wouldn't care what you say about anybody. He's the best. Whatever -- of course I mean everybody can't do everything, you know.
